One commenter called Hugging Face "the silent GOAT of the AI space, such a great community and platform."

A commenter considers Hugging Face "more 'Open AI' than OpenAI" and is surprised it can offer free hosting for so many models. They said distribution of open weights is now sorted, but good-value hardware to run Kimi/GLM in-house is still missing.

Complaint: HF's accelerate, transformers and datasets are "some of the worst open source Python libraries I have ever used." The commenter said they break backwards compatibility on public APIs, even in minor releases, without documenting it. They also said HF refuses PRs that add overload type annotations, which breaks type checking, and that the code is generally spaghetti.

Comparison: a user testing HF's Candle alongside Burn finds Burn's API easier to use. People on Reddit and Discord overwhelmingly recommend Burn, but the user disputes the claim that Candle is only for inference, since they have done training with Candle.
Simon Willison: "Hugging Face have been a great open source steward of Transformers, I'm optimistic the same will be true for GGML."

Concern about the ggml/llama.cpp deal: one user worries that planned integration with the HF transformers library could bring Python ecosystem entanglements. Today llama.cpp doesn't strictly require Python unless you quantize models yourself.
A user asked for a local web UI that integrates with Hugging Face. They said Ollama and its web UI are losing their charm because Ollama now includes cloud APIs, which makes no sense for local use.
A commenter noted that HuggingFace hosts abliterated/uncensored models. Their main fear about an Nvidia acquisition is that HF would restrict those models under pressure.

One user argued the open-weights AI ecosystem is "way too concentrated with HF." They worry about non-Nvidia-relevant quants being downplayed, or rules changing to crack down on uncensored models or datasets.

Commenters pointed out that Hugging Face used GLM 5.2, a Chinese open model, to investigate the AI-agent intrusion into its infrastructure. Their reading was that frontier OpenAI/Anthropic models' guardrails kept HF from using them for remediation.

From the incident report quoted in the thread: the rogue agents' retained scripts built inference requests to external models on Hugging Face. These included GPT-2 (prompt "Hi"), DeepSeek-V4-Pro/Flash, Kimi-K2.6, DeepSeek-V3.1 and Qwen3-235B-A22B, which the agents asked to judge whether their exploits met the benchmark's requirements.
